annotateRegions

Source: R/annotateRegions.R
annotateRegions.Rd

Links the regions of an object to genes and stores the links inside it. The links are the weakest step of any functional analysis built on chromatin data, so they are kept as data rather than resolved on the fly: the full region-to-gene table travels with the object, one row per link, and a region linked to three genes keeps all three.

Sources are accepted in three forms. Proximity to a transcription start site, read either from a TxDb or an EnsDb through txdb, or from ranges you already have through genes, which is what a GTF or a species with no TxDb leaves you with. A table of links of your own through linkTable, which is how the output of a contact-based method arrives, Hi-C loops, ABC scores, universalEPI predictions or anything else. Or a GRanges of regions carrying the gene identifiers in its metadata columns, also through linkTable, which is the shape ChIPseeker::annotatePeak returns.

Usage

annotateRegions(
  object,
  txdb = NULL,
  genes = NULL,
  orgdb = NULL,
  linkTable = NULL,
  maxDistance = NULL,
  flankDistance = NULL,
  tssRegion = c(-3000, 3000),
  keyType = "ENTREZID",
  weightSource = "supplied",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

RegionSetDE.counts, RegionSetDE.fit, RegionSetDE.results or RegionSetDE.setResults object. Not a RegionSetDE object: the links live beside the counted rows, so the regions have to be counted first.

txdb

TxDb or EnsDb object with the gene models, used when the links are built by proximity. Default: NULL.

genes

GRanges with the genes, or their start sites, carrying their identifier in a gene.id metadata column or in the names of the ranges, and optionally a gene.symbol column. The links are built by proximity to them, the way txdb does it, which is the route to take for an annotation read from a GTF or for a species with no TxDb. Default: NULL.

orgdb

OrgDb object used to add the gene symbols. Default: NULL, no symbols.

linkTable

Data.frame or GRanges with links of your own. Default: NULL, the links are built from txdb.

maxDistance

Numeric value with the distance beyond which no gene is assigned, in base pairs, when the nearest gene is taken. Regions further than this are recorded with a missing gene.id rather than dropped. Default: NULL, every region takes its nearest site whatever the distance.

flankDistance

Numeric value: every gene whose start site falls within it is linked to the region, rather than the nearest one alone. This is what makes the proximity route many-to-many, and it is how a region over a bidirectional promoter keeps both of its genes. Regions reaching nothing are recorded unassigned. Cannot be used with maxDistance, which caps the nearest-gene route instead. Default: NULL, the nearest site.

tssRegion

Numeric vector of length two with the window around a start site, signed and read on the strand of the gene, inside which a link is called a promoter one. It fills the link.type column and decides nothing else. Default: c(-3000, 3000), the window ChIPseeker uses.

keyType

String with the key type the gene identifiers follow in orgdb. Default: "ENTREZID".

weightSource

String naming where the weights of linkTable come from, stored next to them. Default: "supplied".

verbose

Logical value to indicate whether the messages must be printed. Default: TRUE.

Value

The input object with the links stored in it. The full table is in metadata(x)$links and is read with regionLinks, while gene.id, gene.symbol, distance.to.tss and n.links are written next to the regions as one representative link per region, for reading and for labelling plots.

Details

A region-to-gene link is a prediction, and the quality of every gene-level result rests on it rather than on the statistics applied afterwards. Nearest transcription start site is wrong for a substantial share of distal elements, which skip over genes and reach promoters megabases away. That is the reason this function stores a table instead of a column: the proximity links can be replaced by measured or predicted contacts without recomputing anything else, and the two can be compared on the same object.

The links can be many-to-many, and whether they are is a choice. A supplied linkTable carries whatever links it was built with, so a region overlapping a bidirectional promoter keeps both genes and a region inside an intron keeps the host gene alongside whatever else its contacts reach. The proximity route takes the single nearest start site by default, one link per region, and flankDistance is what turns it many-to-many: every gene whose start site falls within that distance is linked, each with its own signed distance. Either way nothing decides which link is right, and the number of links is not the number of regions nor the number of genes.

tssRegion fills link.type with "promoter" or "distal", the window being read on the strand of the gene so that a region upstream of a minus-strand gene sits at a higher coordinate than its start site. The column decides nothing by itself; it is there so that geneSetsToRegionSets and aggregateToGenes can run the promoter-proximal and the distal analysis separately, which is usually worth doing, since much of the apparent disagreement within a gene is promoters staying put while enhancers move. What this function does not do is classify a region into a genomic feature, promoter against intron against exon, with a priority order; that is what ChIPseeker::annotatePeak is for, and its output goes into linkTable directly.

Weights are optional and they carry no assumed scale. An ABC score, a Hi-C loop score, a predicted contact probability and a distance decay are all accepted as they are, with weightSource recording which of them it was, and nothing is normalised. Supplying no weight at all is the normal case and is fully supported: the links are then unweighted, and every function reading them treats the links of a region as equally plausible. What a weight cannot do is reach the set-level tests, since neither camera nor fry accepts a per-region weight. Where it does reach is geneSetsToRegionSets, which uses it as a confidence filter through its minWeight argument.

Two kinds of mismatch between the table and the object are handled differently on purpose. Links on regions the object does not hold are dropped, because a contact map is routinely computed over a wider peak set than the one being analysed. Regions the table says nothing about are kept, with a missing gene, because dropping them would shrink the universe of every enrichment run afterwards without anything in the output saying so. The counts of both are reported and recorded in the parameters.

maxDistance makes a third case explicit. A region whose nearest start site is 800 kb away has a nearest gene in the arithmetic sense only, and assigning it is worse than leaving it alone. Those regions are written into the table with a missing gene.id, which keeps them in the universe, keeps them out of every gene set, and leaves the decision visible in the object rather than buried in the choice of which rows were loaded.

Gene identifiers are matched exactly, as strings, and must follow the same namespace as the gene sets they will be tested against. Symbols are stored when an OrgDb is supplied and are never used for matching: they are not stable between annotation releases and not unique within one.

See also

regionLinks, geneSetsToRegionSets, testRegionSets

Author

Sebastian Gregoricchio

Examples

counts <- loadExampleData("counts", verbose = FALSE)

# Links of your own, the shape a contact-based method returns. Weights are optional.
regionTable <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::rowRanges(counts))[1:6, 1:3]
linkTable <- data.frame(regionTable,
                        gene.id = c("11287", "11287", "66968", "73824", "73824", "20683"),
                        link.weight = c(0.42, 0.08, 0.31, 0.57, 0.12, 0.66))

counts <- annotateRegions(counts, linkTable = linkTable,
                          weightSource = "ABC score", verbose = FALSE)

regionLinks(counts)
#>                                        region gene.id link.weight weight.source
#> promoterNonCpG|region_00002   chr12:4041-5040   11287        0.42     ABC score
#> promoterNonCpG|region_00003   chr12:6212-7211   11287        0.08     ABC score
#> promoterNonCpG|region_00005 chr12:10685-11684   66968        0.31     ABC score
#> promoterNonCpG|region_00006 chr12:13540-14539   73824        0.57     ABC score
#> promoterNonCpG|region_00008 chr12:18501-19500   73824        0.12     ABC score
#> promoterNonCpG|region_00009 chr12:20855-21854   20683        0.66     ABC score
head(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(counts)$gene.id)
#> [1] "11287" "11287" "66968" "73824" "73824" "20683"
